**Conjugacy means Bayesian updating stays within a convenient distribution family.** Multiply prior density by likelihood, collect terms, and the posterior has the same functional form with updated parameters. This permits exact algebraic updates under the chosen model. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

For a Beta prior and Bernoulli outcomes, successes and failures update two counts. Dirichlet–categorical updating adds category counts. A Gamma prior with Poisson observations updates shape by total counts and rate by exposure. A Gaussian prior with known observation variance combines precisions and precision-weighted means.

**Sufficient statistics make streaming updates compact.** A fixed-dimensional scalar model may need only a few running totals, avoiding storage of every observation or an MCMC run after each event.

But “constant time” is not dimension-free. A K-category distribution stores K parameters; multivariate covariance operations can be substantial. Conjugacy also does not validate the likelihood: a neat Beta update can be confidently misleading if observations are dependent or the rate drifts. Analytical tractability is a computational benefit whose statistical assumptions still need checking.

**Technical details and references.**

Conjugacy means prior times likelihood has the same distributional family as the prior. Beta–Bernoulli updates add successes/failures; Dirichlet–categorical updates add category counts; a Gamma(shape, rate) prior with Poisson counts adds total counts to shape and total exposure to rate. Gaussian observations with known variance add precision and precision-weighted observations to a Gaussian prior. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

For a scalar observation with fixed-dimensional sufficient statistics, these updates can be constant time per event and need no MCMC. The blanket $O(1)$ claim is false when dimension grows: storing a K-category posterior takes $O(K)$ space, and multivariate Gaussian covariance updates involve matrix operations. Conjugacy gives analytical tractability, not dimension-free computation. The posterior is exact only under the selected likelihood/prior assumptions, which still require validation.
